official.application_cycle: Round-based; Round 21 closed 16 January 2026; applications for Round 22 are expected to open in the final quarter of 2026
official.status_note: DFAT states that Australia Awards Fellowships Round 21 is now closed for applications (closed 16 January 2026, 11:59pm AEDT; outcomes notified from August 2026) and that applications for Round 22 are expected to open in the final quarter of 2026.
official.funding_period: per Fellow (competitive grant cap, max 15 per application)
benefits: Funding of up to $34,500 per Fellow is offered on a competitive basis, to a maximum of 15 Fellows per application

Funding supports return air travel and relevant in-Australia travel, training costs, accommodation and living expenses, medical insurance costs when in Australia, special assistance for people with disability, and a program overhead fee
Activities can include a combination of short-term study and/or training, research, professional attachments, and networking
Australian Host Organisations must demonstrate commitment to the program by providing a co-contribution to the Fellowship costs, which can be cash or in-kind
Fellowships provide short-term in-Australia study, research and professional development activities hosted by Australian organisations, but do not lead to academic qualifications
eligibility: Open to applications from eligible Australian organisations from all sectors, including private enterprise, not-for-profit organisations, universities and tertiary institutions, research institutions, Non-Government Organisations and peak industry bodies
Australian Organisations must apply in partnership with Overseas Counterpart Organisations in eligible developing countries; individuals and international organisations cannot apply
Fellows must be a minimum of 18 years of age at the time of commencing the Fellowship

Fellows must not be Australian citizens or be applying for Australian citizenship (this includes dual citizenship where one of the citizenships is Australian), and must not have Australian permanent resident status or be applying for Australian permanent residency
Fellows must not be married or engaged to, or be a de facto of a person who holds, or is eligible to hold, Australian or New Zealand citizenship or permanent residency

Fellows must have been working in their country of citizenship or residency and in an area relevant to the Fellowship activities preceding the date of the proposed commencement, be able to satisfy all Department of Home Affairs visa requirements, and be able to participate for the full duration proposed by the Australian Host Organisation
requirements: Applications must be developed and delivered in accordance with the guidelines for the current round
Australian organisations must provide a co-contribution to Fellowship costs, which can be cash or in-kind
Organisations are limited to submitting six applications on the same ABN, and funding can be requested for up to 15 Fellows per application
In-Australia activities must include a minimum of two weeks, and the duration of in-partner country activities must not exceed the duration of activities in Australia
Successful applicants must nominate Fellows and Reserve Fellows and provide a detailed breakdown of budget line items in the Supplementary Information Form

Australian Host Organisations must submit a Financial Acquittal Statement with a transaction listing and invoices for audit and acquittal, and every Fellow must complete the mandatory online Fellowship Completion Survey
documents: Online application submitted by the Australian organisation through SmartyGrants (an Australian Business Number is required)
Australian Host Organisation legal entity details and current ABN
Overseas Counterpart Organisation details and evidence of the partnership
Fellowship overview/activity plan and proposed budget on DFAT's budget table
Evidence of the mandatory co-contribution (cash or in-kind)
Supplementary Information Form with Fellow nominations and detailed budget breakdown, required from successful applicants
selection_criteria: Stage 1: the Australia Awards Global Support Unit conducts eligibility checks on applications
Stage 2: applications go through assessment and moderation in a competitive selection process

Funded programs are framed around DFAT priority areas: climate change, adaptation, resilience and green energy transition; health; digital economy, cyber resilience and media engagement; gender equality, disability equity and social inclusion; and maritime and the blue economy
Successful Australian Host Organisations should consult the relevant DFAT post in their selection of candidates for Fellowships
coverage: Return air travel and relevant in-Australia travel
Medical insurance costs when in Australia
Special assistance for people with disability
application_method: Online application submitted by the Australian organisation through the DFAT SmartyGrants portal (individuals are not eligible to apply)
After a successful application, Fellows and Reserve Fellows are nominated through the Supplementary Information Form
official.application_route: Australian organisations with an ABN apply online through the DFAT Australia Awards Fellowships SmartyGrants portal, in partnership with an Overseas Counterpart Organisation; individuals and overseas organisations cannot apply.
official.study_mode: Full-time participation in the Fellowship activities for the full duration
official.citizenship_residency: Fellows must be citizens of, and working in, an eligible ODA developing country; Australian citizens, dual nationals holding Australian citizenship, and Australian permanent residents or applicants for permanent residency are excluded, as are people married, engaged or de facto to an Australian or New Zealand citizen or permanent resident.
official.international_eligibility: Fellows come from ODA-eligible developing countries and are nominated by an Australian host organisation; individual applications from overseas are not accepted.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Fellowship activities are framed around DFAT development priority areas (climate change, adaptation, resilience and green energy transition; health; digital economy, cyber resilience and media engagement; gender equality, disability equity and social inclusion; maritime and the blue economy), and Fellows must come from an Overseas Counterpart Organisation in an ODA-eligible country.
official.duration: 2-52 weeks, commencing in Australia and followed by in-partner country activities; the in-partner country duration must not exceed the duration of activities in Australia, and in-Australia activities must include a minimum of two weeks
official.description: The Australia Awards Fellowships program is a competitive grants program providing short-term development opportunities in Australia that develop influential networks to advance development outcomes in partner countries. Fellowship activities aim to provide access to high-quality training, exchange of expertise, skills and knowledge, and opportunities to enhance networks on issues of shared interest.
official.program_type: Competitive grants program for short-term development fellowships hosted by Australian organisations

tuition_coverage: funding supports 'training costs' but no tuition figure is published, and DFAT states Fellowships do not lead to academic qualifications
english_requirement: no English proficiency requirement appears in DFAT's published Fellowship eligibility list
funding amount for Round 22 specifically: the $34,500 cap is published on the program page and in the Round 20 fact sheet; Round 22 guidelines are not yet released
verification.notes: All values taken from DFAT's own domain (program page, applying page, Round 21 guidelines PDF, Round 21 industry briefing PDF, Round 20 fact sheet PDF) and DFAT's official SmartyGrants application portal; direct page fetches failed with repeated transport errors, so content was read as verbatim excerpts from the official dfat.gov.au domain via search.

applicant_utility.summary: No individual can apply for this program: an Australian organisation with an ABN applies to host you through its Overseas Counterpart Organisation, and DFAT funds up to AUD 34,500 per Fellow (maximum 15 Fellows per application) covering return air travel, in-Australia travel, training costs, accommodation and living expenses, medical insurance and program overheads. Fellowships run 2-52 weeks and must include at least two weeks of in-Australia activity, with the Australian host required to add its own cash or in-kind co-contribution. Round 21 closed on 16 January 2026 and Round 22 is expected to open in the final quarter of 2026.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Mid-career and senior officials in ODA-eligible countries whose employer already has, or can build, a partnership with an Australian organisation able to carry the application and co-funding.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your prospective host is an Australian organisation with a current ABN, because the SmartyGrants form is ABN-only and rejects individuals outright

Map your own status against the Fellow rules: 18 or older at commencement, no Australian citizenship or permanent residency including dual citizenship or pending applications, and no marriage, engagement or de facto relationship with an Australian or New Zealand citizen or permanent resident
Line up evidence of relevant work in your country of citizenship or residency immediately before the proposed commencement date
Be certain you can commit to the full duration in Australia, since whole-duration participation is a hard eligibility rule and Fellows are only nominated after the host's application succeeds
Have the host confirm the budget sits within the AUD 34,500 per-Fellow cap and that its mandatory co-contribution is documented in cash or in kind
Watch for Round 22 opening in the final quarter of 2026 and ask your host organisation whether it intends to apply and how it will choose nominees
common_rejection_risks: Applying as an individual or through an overseas organisation, which DFAT states are not eligible to apply
Family or citizenship ties that breach the Australian and New Zealand citizenship and permanent-residency exclusions
A host that cannot evidence its mandatory cash or in-kind co-contribution, or that lodges more than six applications on one ABN or requests more than 15 Fellows
A nominated Fellow who cannot satisfy Department of Home Affairs visa requirements or cannot stay for the full duration
An activity plan with fewer than two weeks in Australia, or an in-partner-country component longer than the in-Australia component
Budget lines outside the published cost categories, or a missing acquittal trail when the grant is later audited
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Anything above the AUD 34,500 per-Fellow cap falls to the Australian host organisation through its mandatory co-contribution; the published funding covers travel, training, accommodation and living expenses, medical insurance, disability assistance and overheads, with no provision for costs outside those categories.
document_audit: The ABN is the gatekeeper: without a current Australian Business Number the host cannot open the application at all
The activity plan and budget must follow the round guidelines and DFAT's own budget table before submission
After a successful application the host must complete a Supplementary Information Form nominating Fellows and reserve Fellows with a detailed budget breakdown

Acquittal is unforgiving: a Financial Acquittal Statement within 30 days of completion supported by a transaction listing and invoices for audit, plus the mandatory online Fellowship Completion Survey for every Fellow
alerts: Round 21 closed at 11:59pm AEDT on 16 January 2026; Round 22 is only expected to open in the final quarter of 2026, so timings can move
Round 21 outcomes are notified from August 2026 and activity windows run to March 2028, meaning Fellows travel long after the application round closes
Fellows are nominated by the host only after it wins funding, so your personal timeline depends on the host's internal selection and its Supplementary Information Form
Applications are capped at six per ABN and 15 Fellows per application, so competition among an organisation's own proposals is real
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Australian organisation applies via SmartyGrants (Stage 1 eligibility checks, Stage 2 assessment and moderation); successful hosts then nominate Fellows and reserve Fellows through the Supplementary Information Form, run the activity, and acquit funds with invoices within 30 days of completion.

official.application_cycle: Semester 1, 2027 offer rounds close 17 August 2026, 5 October 2026 and 16 November 2026; Semester 2, 2027 rounds close 15 February 2027, 22 March 2027 and 3 May 2027, with an additional offer round for International Baccalaureate graduates after 16 December 2026 results and for International UAC students after the 23 December 2026 offer round
official.status_note: No application is required: eligible students who have secured an unconditional offer of admission by a round close date are automatically considered, and the scholarship is offered subject to the availability of funds.
official.funding_period: one year (top tiers) or one semester, by rank
benefits: Five scholarship amounts are offered based on ranking against the selection criteria: $60,000 or $40,000 payable for one year in two equal instalments per semester, and $20,000, $10,000 or $5,000 payable for one semester
For 2026 intakes the scheme includes an additional scholarship value of $60,000
Students who receive a Sydney International Student Award can only receive a VCIS to the maximum value of $40,000
The availability of some amounts may be limited to specified cohorts
The scholarship is awarded once during the first year of commencement and is not renewable for following years; payment is made on or after the relevant census date
eligibility: Applicants must be an international student as defined in the Higher Education Support Act 2003

Applicants must have applied for but not yet commenced a bachelor's degree or a coursework master's degree that is a CRICOS registered award program usually delivered onshore at the University of Sydney
Applicants must receive an unconditional offer of admission by the relevant close date
Applicants commencing a second degree at the University of Sydney are eligible provided they have not previously held the Vice Chancellor's International Scholarships
Recipients of scholarships provided by the Australian Government are not eligible
requirements: Applicants must complete acceptance of their unconditional offer by the relevant deadline associated with their scholarship offer round, and remain enrolled after census date
The payment will be made on or after the relevant census date, and no other amount is payable
The scholarship is offered subject to the availability of funds, and deferral or suspension is not permitted except in exceptional circumstances
Recipients of a scholarship split into two payments must maintain a minimum semester average mark (SAM) of 65 and have no outstanding fees to receive their next payment
Recipients undertaking an exchange during the tenure of the scholarship must have achieved a Satisfied Requirements (SR) grade to receive their next payment

The scholarship terminates if the recipient withdraws or fails to enrol, becomes a domestic student, commences part-time study without prior approval, does not maintain satisfactory academic performance, commits serious misconduct, or accepts another University of Sydney scholarship exceeding A$20,000 per annum
documents: No scholarship-specific documents and no separate application form: consideration is automatic from the admission application
Application for admission to an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree at the University of Sydney
Acceptance of the unconditional offer by the deadline associated with the relevant offer round
selection_criteria: Awarded on the basis of academic merit as assessed from the student's application for admission to an undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree
Awarded on the nomination of a selection committee consisting of two nominees of the Executive Director, Sydney Future Students and one nominee of the Admissions Office
Five scholarship amounts are offered based on the student's ranking against the selection criteria, with availability of some amounts limited to specified cohorts
coverage: $60,000 and $40,000 tiers payable for one year in two equal instalments per semester; $20,000, $10,000 and $5,000 tiers payable for one semester
application_method: No application is required: all eligible students who have secured an unconditional offer of admission by the closing dates are automatically considered
official.application_route: No separate application: apply for admission, secure an unconditional offer by a round close date, and consideration for the scholarship is automatic.
official.study_mode: Full-time undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree; part-time study only with prior approval
official.citizenship_residency: Must be an international student as defined in the Higher Education Support Act 2003.
official.international_eligibility: Yes, the scheme is open exclusively to international students.
official.duration: Awarded once during the first year of commencement: $60,000 and $40,000 tiers payable for one year in two equal instalments per semester; $20,000, $10,000 and $5,000 tiers payable for one semester; not renewable for following years
official.description: The Vice-Chancellor's International Scholarships are awarded to exceptional international students. The VCIS is a scholarship offered on commencement of a coursework degree, awarded once during the first year of commencement and not renewable for following years, with up to $60,000 offered to support high-achieving international students to pursue coursework studies at the University of Sydney.
official.program_type: Merit-based scholarship for commencing international coursework students

not_confirmed: living_cost_coverage: the scheme page publishes award amounts and payment timing but does not state that living costs are covered
tuition_coverage: the scheme page does not state which costs the payment is applied to (it publishes only amounts, instalments and census-date timing)
travel_coverage: no travel benefit is published for this scheme
english_requirement: no English test or MOI requirement is published on the scheme page; English requirements attach separately to admission
verification.notes: The University of Sydney scheme page was fetched in full on 2026-10-10; award values, tiers, round close dates, selection process and termination terms were confirmed from the University's own page.

applicant_utility.summary: You cannot apply for this scholarship and nothing you submit for it counts: an internal committee ranks your admission application on academic merit and awards one of five amounts from $5,000 to $60,000, paid in semester instalments on or after census date. To be in the running you must be an international student who has applied for, but not yet commenced, an onshore CRICOS-registered bachelor's or coursework master's at the University of Sydney and already holds an unconditional offer by a round close date. The award is a one-off made in your first year of commencement and cannot be renewed, deferred or suspended except in exceptional circumstances.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving international students commencing an undergraduate or coursework master's at the University of Sydney who can convert their application into an unconditional offer early.
application_readiness_checklist: Make your admission application as strong as possible, because it is the entire basis of ranking and there is no separate submission to polish

Hold an unconditional offer before the round close date you are targeting: Semester 1, 2027 rounds close 17 August 2026, 5 October 2026 and 16 November 2026; Semester 2, 2027 rounds close 15 February, 22 March and 3 May 2027
Accept the unconditional offer by the deadline attached to your scholarship offer round and stay enrolled past census date, since that is what triggers payment
If you are in line for a two-instalment award, plan for a minimum semester average mark of 65 with no outstanding fees before the second instalment

Audit your other funding first: Australian Government scholarship holders are excluded, a Sydney International Student Award caps your VCIS at $40,000, and accepting another University of Sydney scholarship above $20,000 a year terminates it

IB and International UAC applicants are considered in post-release rounds, after 16 December 2026 IB results and the 23 December 2026 UAC offer round, so their effective deadline is later than the printed round dates
common_rejection_risks: Waiting for a scholarship application that never comes, and arriving at census date with a conditional offer instead of an unconditional one
Missing the round close date for your intake, which removes you from that round's ranking entirely
Withdrawing, failing to enrol, switching to part-time study without prior approval, or becoming a domestic student, all of which are explicit termination triggers
Stacking another University of Sydney scholarship worth more than $20,000 per year, which terminates the VCIS outright
Expecting the award to repeat in later years, or assuming deferral is available if you need to postpone
Counting on a specific tier, since some amounts are limited to specified cohorts and the whole scheme is subject to availability of funds
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The published terms set out only the scholarship value and payment timing and describe no living allowance, travel or other costs, so living expenses and everything beyond the awarded amount remain your responsibility. The scheme page also does not state which costs the payment is applied to, so confirm this in your letter of offer before you budget.
document_audit: There are no scholarship documents to submit, so the audit surface is your admission file and your enrolment status
Your offer must read unconditional by the round close date, since a conditional offer does not enter the ranking
Diarise the offer acceptance deadline, census date and instalment conditions against your own round rather than a generic scheme deadline
If you go on exchange during the award, a Satisfied Requirements grade is needed to keep the next instalment
alerts: The scheme is offered subject to the availability of funds, so eligibility earns you consideration rather than an award
Some scholarship amounts may be limited to specified cohorts, so the tier you are ranked for may not be open to your program or intake

Rules changed from 2026 intakes: a new $60,000 tier was added and the termination threshold for holding another University scholarship rose from $10,000 to $20,000, so check the version that applies to your commencement year
The award is not renewable and is made once in your first year, so do not plan later years of study around it
International Baccalaureate and International UAC applicants are judged in separate later offer rounds
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply for admission, secure an unconditional offer by a round close date, receive automatic consideration and committee ranking, accept the scholarship offer by its deadline, stay enrolled past census date, then receive payment on or after census date.
